newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends higher amid low dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends higher amid low dlr demand.

text.p: The Philippine peso stretched last week's gains on Monday to close at 26.322 from 26.331 amid low dollar demand from oil companies for the week, traders said.
Two oil firms have so far indicated they would buy a total of $57.3 million for the week.
"People were expecting $150 million (this week)," a foreign bank dealer said.
That led to the sell-off of dollars and prompted the Central Bank to intervene in the afternoon, dealer said.

Traders said the peso was also helped by stock market inflows and remarks made by Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo over the weekend in Thailand that the country had no plan to depreciate the peso to help boost exports.
The Central Bank was estimated to have bought $42 million at 26.321 and 26.323.
The peso averaged at 26.323 for the day versus 26.331 against the dollar. Volume rose to $209.3 million from $$187.20 million.
